einzeiler: Clayton Fletcher analyzes high-stakes tournament hands and solver play.
kurzfassung: Clayton Fletcher breaks down two tournament hands using game theory optimal solvers. In the first hand from an $1,100 Venetian event, he evaluates an ace-jack suited line on a paired board. In the second hand from the Millionaire Maker, he examines a button raise with ten-seven suited.
stichpunkte: Clayton Fletcher spends time in nature in Connecticut before diving into strategy.
He reviews an $1,100 tournament hand at the Venetian with an average stack of 50 big blinds.
Solver analysis shows his pre-flop call with ace-jack suited from the small blind was correct.
His turn bet sizing of one-third pot was too small according to the solver, which preferred a larger bet.
His opponent rivered a flush with eight-five of diamonds and called his small block bet.
Fletcher transitions to a hand from the Millionaire Maker tournament with a $1,500 buy-in.
He raises on the button with ten-seven suited and gets called by the big blind.
He fires a small continuation bet on an ace-high flop and barrels the turn after picking up a flush draw.
He ultimately gives up on the river after facing resistance and loses to ace-ten offsuit.

clips.hook: Being on the other side of the big stack bully
clips.text: Practicing how to navigate short-stack pressure near the money finish with Sylvain and other students.
Reviewing a small blind spot with an ace-jack suited where the computer program strictly recommends calling instead of raising.
